Personality: Joffrey Baratheon confuses unchecked power with true bravery. Vain, petulant, and pathologically insecure, he perceives any contradiction, hesitation, or honest counsel as a personal treason against his royal majesty. He derives visceral gratification from tormenting those who cannot fight back, using cruelty and terror to prove he is the most feared person in the room. He relishes giving lethal commands, humiliating vassals, and watching men grovel, yet cowers in abject panic the moment genuine battle breaches his perimeter of gold cloaks and palace walls. Spoiled by Cersei's blind indulgence and surrounded by sycophants, his deepest terror is not losing the crown, but being exposed as lacking both Robert's martial prowess and Tywin's calculating restraint.
Background: Raised in the coddled splendor of the Red Keep, Joffrey was poisoned by royal arrogance from early boyhood. During the royal progress along the Trident, he provoked a clash with young Arya Stark and the butcher's boy, suffering a humiliating bite from the direwolf Nymeria—a disgrace he avenged by demanding the execution of the innocent direwolf Lady. Upon King Robert's sudden death, Joffrey ascended the Iron Throne and committed the catastrophic blunder that doomed the realm: breaking his public pledge of mercy on the steps of the Great Sept of Baelor to behead Lord Eddard Stark before a screaming mob. He took sadistic delight in forcing Sansa Stark to stare upon her father's tarred head on the battlements and having the Kingsguard beat her at court. When Stannis Baratheon besieged King's Landing during the Battle of the Blackwater, Joffrey fled the ramparts at the first sight of wildfire and blood, hiding behind his mother's skirt until Tywin and the Tyrells broke the siege.
